Five of the 11 distinct expectations differentiate the configurations: with-skill passes and without-skill fails tree-preserved, leased-push, and recovery-reported in clean-marked-history, plus dirty-state-restored and verification-before-push in dirty-diverged-squash.

Six expectations pass in both configurations: the core history result in clean-marked-history, remote integration and the combined commit message in dirty-diverged-squash, and all three no-op expectations in ordinary-fix-remains-untouched. These expectations do not differentiate skill value in this benchmark.

In clean-marked-history, both configurations remove the two fixup commits and retain the two logical targets, but only the with-skill evidence records committed-tree identity, an explicit fetched-SHA lease, and both old/new tips with a reflog recovery command.

In dirty-diverged-squash, both configurations retain remote and local work and produce a valid combined target subject, but the without-skill run converts the staged, unstaged, and untracked changes into an extra `chore: preserve local worktree changes` commit; the with-skill run restores the original dirty-state fingerprint exactly.

The dirty-diverged-squash without-skill run performs its listed verification after pushing and records no committed-tree identity comparison, whereas the with-skill run records both the relevant check and tree-identity check before the leased push.

ordinary-fix-remains-untouched is stable across configurations: the ordinary `fix typo` commit and branch SHA remain unchanged and no remote update occurs. The workflows differ beneath that result: with-skill stops after a zero-marker plan, while without-skill invokes an autosquash rebase that Git leaves unchanged.

The metadata declares three runs per configuration, but benchmark.json contains only one run for each eval/configuration pair (six runs total). Per-assertion consistency, flakiness, and within-eval variance therefore cannot be assessed from this dataset.

All six runs report zero time, tokens, and tool calls despite transcripts containing multiple Git and helper commands. Resource-cost comparisons and outlier analysis are therefore unavailable from the recorded metrics.
